verdict: Parker Hannifin posted record first-quarter sales of $6.0B, up 18% — 11.5% of it organic — as demand rose across every market it serves, and it raised its full-year outlook after closing the Filtration Group acquisition.

segments.name: Diversified Industrial
segments.note: Motion and control products for industrial customers — North America $2,445M (+20%) and international $1,707M (+22%), including the acquired Filtration Group business.

segments.name: Aerospace Systems
segments.note: Systems for aircraft and aerospace — 13.9% organic growth and a 26.6% segment operating margin.

segments.name: Corporate — tariff returns
segments.note: Sales were reduced by $27M of IEEPA tariff-related returns to customers, recorded at Corporate.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling and running the company — segment results are after $58M of corporate general and administrative costs.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $146M, partly offset by $87M of other income, net.
follow100Note: Parker kept $14.75 of every $100 of sales as profit. Segment sales total $6,019M before the $27M corporate tariff returns. Rows are rounded to cents.

takeaways.title: Demand, not just deals, drove growth
takeaways.text: Organic sales rose 11.5% with increased demand across all market verticals and record backlog levels. Acquisitions — mainly Filtration Group — added about 7 points of the 18% reported growth.

takeaways.title: Record adjusted margins
takeaways.text: Segment operating margin was 24.4% on a GAAP basis and a record 28.6% adjusted. Aerospace Systems earned a 26.6% GAAP margin on sales up 14%; Diversified Industrial earned 23.4% on sales up 21%.

takeaways.title: The outlook went up
takeaways.text: Parker raised fiscal 2027 guidance: reported sales growth of 16–19%, organic growth of 7.5–10.5%, and adjusted EPS of $36.45 to $37.25 — now including Filtration Group.

oneTimers: Deal costs are inside GAAP profit: $78M of acquisition-related expenses (including the fair-value step-up of acquired inventory), $23M of integration costs to achieve, $17M of business realignment charges and a net $22M tariff-refund adjustment. Excluding these and $189M of amortization of acquired intangibles, adjusted net income was $1,138M ($8.90 per share).
Net sales were reduced by $27M at Corporate for IEEPA tariff-related returns to customers — tariffs a court ruled unauthorized — partly offset by $6M received from the U.S. government.
footerNote: Segment sales total $6,019M; consolidated net sales are $5,992M after $27M of corporate IEEPA tariff-related returns to customers.
